correctness.rationale: The basis product collapses to XY=r_X c_Y^T. The margin map has image all pairs with common total s and has a kernel of dimension d=(m−1)(n−1), as is seen by filling one row and one column. Thus X^h=s^(h−2)rc^T, with the factor interpreted as 1 for a square. For nonzero target total, each scalar root of s^h=t(Z) forces the two margins; for rank one the identity rho(Z) gamma(Z)^T=t(Z)Z proves sufficiency. At zero total, nonzero square targets require both margins zero and have exactly q−1 ordered rank-one factorizations; the same targets cannot be higher powers. The zero-square fiber is the union of the two zero-margin cases, while the higher zero fiber is the total-sum hyperplane. Normalizing one factor to have total 1 gives q^(m+n−2) rank-one targets at every prescribed nonzero total; dividing the ordered nonzero zero-sum factor count by q−1 gives the exceptional cone. These arguments cover m=1 or n=1 and all field characteristics, and give both advertised image counts and the input mass. The accompanying direct basis-law code and 29 recorded finite checks were read, not rerun.

value.rationale: The complete fiber function is a useful exact invariant of the natural power map on a standard nonunital algebra. It distinguishes the scalar cyclic-group obstruction from a separate zero-total cone that is hit by squaring but by no higher power. Both the support and actual multiplicities are needed for power-map counts; the result identifies precisely when this extra support exists, including degenerate rectangles and extension fields. It is more than counting nonzero scalar roots or reporting finite experiments.
